No one has entered appearance on behalf of the respondent no.2 to oppose the prayer for bail.
3. The appellant in this case is seeking suspension of his sentence and release on bail during pendency of the appeal.
4. The appellant has been convicted and sentenced vide judgment and order dated 09.02.2024 and 15.02.2024 Patna High Court CR.

sentences.text: He has been further sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for twenty years with a fine of Rs.5,000/- for the offence under Section 376(AB) IPC and in case of default of payment of fine, he shall further undergo simple imprisonment for three months.
Both the sentences shall run concurrently.
5. As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the appellant is that he had committed rape upon the two victim girls who were minor.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in this case the appellant and the prosecution side both are close- door neighbours.

The appellant was 59 years old at the time of Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.348 of 2024(6) dt.11-09-2024 occurrence and against him it is alleged that he had committed rape on the two victim girls who were minor.
It is submitted that in this case the alleged occurrence is said to have taken place on 01.01.2020.

One of the victims has stated that when she along with her friend Ms. 'X' had gone to Bandh in search of her grandfather, from there this appellant had taken them adjacent to the school where there is only a 'Jungle'.
It is at this place that the appellant is said to have committed sexual penetrative act, gave the victims some coins of 1-2 rupees and told her not to disclose the occurrence to her grandmother.
The victims have stated that the appellant had given a cut by his teeth on the cheek of both the victims.
They came to their house and informwd the occurrence to their mother whereafter the mother of the another victim and her grand parents had also gone to the police station.
The submission is that in this case the written application was submitted in the police station only on 04.01.2020 i.e. after three days of the occurrence and knowledge thereof.

7. Learned counsel submits that, it would appear from the deposition of the two victims that one of them has stated that they had gone to Bandh in search of the grandfather of one of the victims from where this appellant had taken them away but Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.348 of 2024(6)
dt.11-09-2024 the another victim has stated that she was playing at the door of the appellant with her friend when the appellant had given them chocolate and biscuit and took them away behind the school and committed wrong act with them.
It is, thus, submitted that the victims are making two different statements with regard to the place from where they were taken away by the appellant.
The second victim has not stated about giving money.
Nobody had seen them in taking away by the appellant even as it has come in evidence that there were several houses in the vicinity.
8. Learned counsel submits that the reason behind the false implication of the appellant is a land dispute.

When the mother of the victim deposed as PW-10, the defence suggested her that Bhikhari Sah who is full brother of this appellant had purchased a piece of land from Atmaram Sah, who is father-in- law of the co-sharer and Dasrath Sah (the informant) wanted to purchase the said land from Bhikhari Sah, on that issue there was a dispute between the parties.

Although PW-10 denied Chandrika Sah vs The State Of Bihar on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9004301/

sentences.text: When the wife of the informant deposed as PW-11 she has admitted that Atmaram Sah was the co-sharer of this witness and his land was purchased by Bhikhari Sah who is the elder brother of the appellant.
She has also admitted in her cross-examination that her Bhaisur Ram Prasad Sah wanted to Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.348 of 2024(6) dt.11-09-2024 purchase the said land.
9. Learned counsel submits that the witness was also suggestd that the prosecution side had a dispute over right to way with the appellant and his brother.

10. Learned counsel has pointed out from the evidence of the defence witness Bhikhari Sah that he had produced the document of the land in the court which he had purchased from the co-sharer of Dashrath Sah (the informant).
He has deposed in his examination-in-chief that Dashrath Sah (the informant) wanted him to transfer the said land but he had not trnasferred the land and there was a dispute for the same.
It is pointed out that DW-1 has not been cross-examined to demolish the statement that the informant wanted that the said land be transferred to him.

11. Learned counsel has pointed out that the medical evidence which has been brought on the record completely rules out the ocular evidence as neither any sign of rape has been found nor any cut mark on the cheek of the victims could be noticed by the doctor.
The doctor has opined that there was no injury seen and no bleeding was there.
12. It is submitted that when the medical evidence competely rules out the ocular evidence and in fact in respect of one of the victims the doctor has recorded that the hymen was Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.348 of 2024(6) dt.11-09-2024 intact whereas in respect of another it was recorded that the hymen was old tear.
In case of both the victims, there is no whisper in the injury report that there was any sign of rape.
The appellant has remained in custody since 29.01.2020 and this appeal being that of the year 2024 is not likely to be heard in near future.
13. Mr. Parmeshwar Mehta, learned Addl.P.P. for the State has oppssed the prayer of the appellant.
It is submitted that both the victims are minor and they have supported the prosecution case.

14. Having regard to the submissions recorded hereinabove and the materials which we have prima-facie noticed for purpose of consideration of the prayer for bail of the appellant, finding that the victims are giving two different places from where they were allegedly picked-up by the appellant, nobody had seen the appellant taking away both the victims towards the school, the complaint was made in the police station after three days, the medical evidence completely rules out the allegation of rape and no injury at all has been found on any part of the body of the victims as alleged, the defence has prima-facie shown that it may be a case of false implication on account of land dispute, taking note of the further Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.348 of 2024(6)
dt.11-09-2024 material that the appellant is in incarceration for more than four years and the appeal is not likely to be heard in near future, we direct suspension of sentence and release of the appellant on bail, during pendency of the appeal, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/-(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VII-cum-Special Judge, POCSO Court II, Muzaffarpur in connection with G.R.

16. It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only prima-facie and tenative for the purpose of consideration of the prayer of the appellant for suspension of sentence and release on bail only which would not cause prejudice to the either parties.
17. List this appeal for hearing on it's turn.
